title: With Due Respect (Vol. 7) -- Ch. 4: Awesome Gathering Power
keywords: change the course of our history
wisdom and strength over the ages
primary_topics: Chapter 4 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7) -- CJP's July 5, 2009 Inquirer column on the Catholic Church's 'awesome gathering power,' demonstrated when over 12,000 lay faithful filled the SMX for the Congress on Parish Liturgical Life despite the H1N1 scare

His reflection that Cardinal Rosales, like Cardinal Sin in 1986 and 2001, could summon 'an army of faithful' able to 'topple authoritarian and corrupt regimes' -- the 'secret weapon' being Metro Manila's parishes and Catholic schools

His own sharing at the Congress on 'equality before God' -- that as Chief Justice he chose to remain 'an ordinary parishioner' and extraordinary minister at his Makati parish, 'without extra arrangements or protocols'
A closing tribute to Washington Sycip at 88 -- whose birthday gathered the business elite -- as the commercial counterpart to the archbishop's gravitational pull, 'wisdom and strength over the ages'
sub_topics: The demonstration: the Church's gathering power was 'convincingly if quietly demonstrated' when, 'defying the influenza A(H1N1) contagion,' more than 12,000 lay faithful (6,000 per Saturday) 'crowded the Congress on Parish Liturgical Life at the gigantic SMX'

The cut-short vacation: CJP, who each summer travels with his wife to 'out-of-the-way places' (Machu Picchu, the Yellow Mountains, Iguassu, the Canadian Rockies), cut short an Alaska trip to make the Congress, arriving as Gaudencio Cardinal Rosales concluded a keynote met with 'adulating love' and 'prolonged ovation'

Disciplined disciples: though the theme was 'religious, not political,' the 'cheering throng could have warmed up to any topic' and 'been swayed to any direction' -- these were lay leaders of the Archdiocese's '13 vicariates and 92 parishes' (lectors, ministers, altar servers, greeters), 'called to arms' by the Archdiocesan Liturgical Commission

The gathering power: 'gazing at the teeming but disciplined disciples,' CJP was 'convinced that Cardinal Rosales could easily produce more than enough warm bodies to change the course of our history, just as Jaime Cardinal Sin did in 1986 and 2001' -- able 'at any time' to summon 'an army of faithful who could jam the streets... indefinitely'

Residual power: though the Archdiocese was 'sliced into several dioceses' after Sin's death, the Congress showed Rosales's 'residual awesome power' to gather believers 'that can topple authoritarian and corrupt regimes' -- as when, during the NBN-ZTE scandal, the prelate 'openly resisted all proposals for Charter change prior to June 30, 2010,' backed by Msgr. Santos of MAPSA and the 1,252-school CEAP

Sin's secret weapon: CJP identifies the 'lethal combination of parishes and Catholic schools in Metro Manila' as the force Sin wielded for 'People Power I and II' -- a force he believes Rosales 'could wield' for his vision of 'fullness of life' and 'deliverance from anything that enslaves'

Equality before God: he recalls becoming an extraordinary minister of Holy Communion at the Santuario de San Antonio in 1989, and that on becoming Chief Justice he told his parish priest he 'remained an ordinary parishioner' wanting to serve 'without extra arrangements or protocols' -- for 'in serving our Lord... we, the people of God, are all equal'

At the pearly gates: invoking Matthew 25, he writes that the Lord 'will not ask us how many digits were in our bank accounts, or how many doctoral degrees we earned,' but 'whether we shared our resources with the poor, used our talent to defend the weak,' and served humbly -- and closes with a separate tribute to Washington Sycip, whose 88th-birthday gathering of 500 'topmost business stars' made him the commercial match to the archbishop's pull: 'wisdom and strength over the ages'

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 4 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7), CJP's July 5, 2009 Inquirer column, reflects on the Catholic Church's 'awesome gathering power,' shown when -- 'defying the influenza A(H1N1) contagion' -- more than 12,000 lay faithful filled the SMX for the Congress on Parish Liturgical Life. CJP, who cut short an Alaska vacation to attend, arrived as Gaudencio Cardinal Rosales concluded a keynote met with 'adulating love.' Though the theme was 'religious, not political,' he sensed the 'disciplined disciples' (lay leaders of the Archdiocese's 13 vicariates and 92 parishes) 'could have been swayed to any direction,' and was 'convinced that Cardinal Rosales could easily produce more than enough warm bodies to change the course of our history, just as Jaime Cardinal Sin did in 1986 and 2001,' summoning 'an army of faithful' able to 'topple authoritarian and corrupt regimes' -- as the prelate had shown by resisting Charter change amid the NBN-ZTE scandal. The 'secret weapon,' he writes, is 'the lethal combination of parishes and Catholic schools in Metro Manila.' Recalling his own sharing at the Congress, he tells how, on becoming Chief Justice, he chose to remain 'an ordinary parishioner' and extraordinary minister at the Santuario de San Antonio 'without extra arrangements or protocols,' because 'in serving our Lord... we, the people of God, are all equal' -- and, invoking Matthew 25, that at the 'pearly gates' the Lord will ask not about 'bank accounts' or 'doctoral degrees' but 'whether we shared our resources with the poor.' He closes with a tribute to Washington Sycip at 88, whose birthday gathering of 500 business titans made him the commercial counterpart to the archbishop's pull -- 'wisdom and strength over the ages.'
